title: Derivative loss in L4 Strichartz on the cube surface
credit: Blair, Ford, Marzuola, Strichartz estimates for the wave equation on flat cones / Euclidean surfaces with conical singularities, arXiv:1003.0666.
results: s* >= 0 (trivial). No positive lower bound known. s* <= 1/4: Blair-Ford-Marzuola, Thm 1.5 (arXiv 1003.0666), loss 1/p for compact Euclidean surfaces with conical singularities, p=q=4; authors call the loss an artifact of the method.
plain: On the flat torus, the L4 space-time estimate for Schrodinger waves loses only epsilon derivatives (Bourgain). On the surface of a cube, which has eight cone points that diffract waves, only a loss of 1/4 derivative is known. Find the true loss: prove any loss below 1/4, or show some loss is necessary.
math: Let $S$ be the unit cube surface, $\Delta$ the Friedrichs extension from $C_c^\infty(S\setminus\text{vertices})$, and $s^*=\inf\{s\ge0:\|e^{it\Delta}f\|_{L^4([0,1]\times S)}\le C_s\|f\|_{H^s(S)}\}$. Known: $0\le s^*\le\tfrac14$ (Blair–Ford–Marzuola). Prove $s^*<\tfrac14$, or $s^*>0$; ideally determine $s^*$ (conjecturally $0$). The board's target (Claim) is $s^*<\tfrac14$.
